title: connector apps, E4 batch 2 (OAuth): DocuSign as the first declarative verification of the outbound OAuth path, an open-edition metadata package
body:
epic:#27293#1 · sunhaolin · session_017xRBcVBKAFk1ntXSjvPt7U

Blocked-by: #26702

Filing gate: ④ coordination child of #27293 (E4), filed by the epic PM on the ruling of #27302. Ruling-ref: 6486157794 (letter A, phased: "DocuSign for the OAuth path … OAuth after #26702"). Child of #27293. ⛔ Not a claim.

## Why DocuSign

It is the one connector with measured demand: an app-authoring agent on HotCLM concluded the platform had to build a DocuSign plugin (the instance #27223 fixed in the skills; #25747 closed as "a declarative instance once OAuth lands"). #27223's eval already fixes the expected shape.

## Work

- A metadata package: a declarative `provider: 'openapi'` instance over DocuSign's eSignature document normalized by #27373's script (`--empty-consumes application/json` is required for its 187 operations with an empty `consumes`), an `include` of the three operations the eval names (create envelope, get envelope, list status changes), `auth` of the `oauth2` kind #26702 lands, the contract fields and flows, and the listing file plus a README credentials section.
- The callback: DocuSign Connect signs its own header, which the `api` door does not verify; poll status until vendor callback schemes are supported, and say so in the README.
- Validated by this repository's CI at HEAD; one live sandbox round trip run once locally and reported.

## Reader

The epic PM of #27293 dispatches it when #26702 closes (the server lane holds #26702: blocked on its spec slice, comment 6524351146). Home: the same directory batch 1 (#28276) settles.
